p-list.p-item: Added Cheats: create custom cheat codes, enable them in game, and browse built-in cheat templates for supported platforms.
Added cheat template search and automatic template matching: RetroGo can use a ROM's CRC32 to look up game metadata and bind a matching cheat template when available.
Cheat templates are now delivered as an optional On-Demand Resource, keeping the base app smaller while allowing the full offline cheat database to be downloaded when needed.
Improved the Discover page by grouping different variants of the same game into one entry, making game browsing cleaner and less repetitive.
Added Chinese game names to the Discover database, so game titles can follow the app language while still preserving authoritative English names where useful.
Improved in-game synchronization with the new GamePauseCoordinator, making menus, sheets, and game resume timing more reliable.
Added a customizable in-game toolbar: rearrange, pin, or hide the top buttons, with the rest tucked into a More menu — set up the in-game bar exactly the way you like it.
Added a landscape lock button to keep the game fixed in landscape while you play.
The entire app now rotates with your device — every screen follows the device orientation, not just the game.
Added Turbo speed levels — Very Slow, Slow, Medium, Fast, Very Fast — configurable per core, and per game.
Added a tap-to-lock Turbo option for the X/Y buttons: a quick tap keeps auto-fire running hands-free, tap again to release — also configurable per core, and per game.
Improved the in-game toolbar icons with subtle shadows so they stay clearly visible even over bright or white game scenes.
Added a Contact Us option in Settings to send feedback by email.
Added in-game disc switching support for multidisc games, including M3U-based game sets.
Added an Acknowledgments page to credit open-source projects, Libretro contributors, and homebrew games used in RetroGo promotional materials.
Introduced a Game Discovery tab powered by On-Demand Resources, letting you browse and look up game information across multiple platforms directly inside the app.
Redesigned the app navigation with a Tab Bar — Library, Discover, and Settings now each live in their own tab for faster access and a cleaner layout.

Overhauled the game library with a fully rearchitected file browser: each page represents a folder in your library, with four view modes — flat icon grid, flat list, grouped by core, grouped by tag, and a tree outline for a full folder hierarchy at a glance.
Added distinctive platform icons for each game system so your library is easier to scan at a glance, along with refined iconography throughout the rest of the app.
Fixed a Turbo button conflict in the custom RetroArch key mapping that prevented acceleration from working correctly in PSP racing games.
Introduced RetroGo Pro to support continued development, with monthly, yearly, and lifetime unlock options.
Added feature access management for Pro-only functionality.
Added per-player external controller mapping with in-app binding configuration.
Added persistent game-level input binding profiles, automatically restored per ROM.
Added configurable core/game options: video driver, audio driver, and mute during fast-forward.
Added overlay touch player assignment and improved virtual/physical input coordination.
Improved stability for Saturn (Yabause) when exiting with connected controllers.
Refactored the runtime architecture by separating RetroArch rendering and game logic, with game logic now running on an independent thread for improved frame stability and responsiveness.
Added fast-forward support with 2x / 3x / 4x / 6x speed levels, reducing repetitive wait time and improving gameplay efficiency.
Integrated signalsmith-stretch for audio smoothing during fast-forward, effectively reducing noise artifacts and improving overall listening quality.
Upgraded configuration to a dual-layer model (core-level + game-level): set defaults per core and override them per game for finer-grained personalization.
Added a new SpriteKit-based Overlay buttons system to improve the in-game control and interaction experience.
Added smart multi-file ROM import detection for both file import and folder import workflows.
The importer can now automatically recognize grouped game files such as cue, m3u, gdi, mds, and ccd, detect missing referenced files, and handle grouped imports more reliably.
Enhanced data security by migrating core files (Roms, Save States, Databases, etc.) to a secure system directory, preventing accidental deletion and ensuring a more stable app experience.
RetroGo was officially released on the App Store.
